overview: Tenacity 6.0's Criticals makes melee attacks land as crits by queueing C03 position-lift packets that claim a small upward offset with onGround false before the attack, so the server-side entity carries fall distance when the C02 arrives. The Watchdog mode (default) fires on every grounded MotionEvent and queues two lifts, 0.06 plus random jitter and 0.01 plus random jitter; the Packet mode gates three sub-pixel lifts, 0.006253453, 0.002253453 and 0.001253453, behind an on-ground target check and a hurt-resistance threshold. The Dev mode is present only as commented-out source that would add a fourth lift and a C18PacketSpectate with a random UUID. The module never sends the attack itself; it services the player's normal C02 clicks by pre-arming the fall distance.

sections.p: Watchdog runs from the MotionEvent listener with no attack gating at all: whenever e.isOnGround() is true it queues two C04PacketPlayerPosition packets at the current position plus 0.06 plus a random value below 0.001, and the same plus 0.01 plus jitter, both with onGround false. Because the event fires every tick while the player is grounded, the mode produces a continuous two-lift-per-tick stream that keeps the server-side fall distance nonzero at all times. The 0.06 lift is above the 1.8 minimum-move threshold of 0.03, so the server actually moves the entity up, while the 0.01 lift sits below it and only applies the onGround flag.

Packet mode adds three conditions before lifting: the object mouse-over must target an entity, the local player must be onGround, and the target's hurtResistantTime must exceed the Delay setting (default 1, range 0-20). When those hold it queues three C04 lifts at 0.006253453, 0.002253453 and 0.001253453, all below the 0.03 min-move, so the server ignores the coordinate deltas but applies the onGround false flag to each. The mode therefore produces the flag-only ground spoof signature rather than a visible position change, and the Delay setting doubles as the hurt-time threshold that spaces lift bursts around the hittable window.

The Dev branch is fully commented out: it would queue four offsets up to 0.06253453 and then a C18PacketSpectate carrying a random UUID, a spectate packet that has no business in a criticals module and is the kind of leftover that points at a paste lineage. The TimerUtil field timer is declared but never referenced anywhere in the file, and PacketUtils is imported yet only the dead Dev branch would call sendPacketNoEvent; the live modes queue through mc.thePlayer.sendQueue.addToSendQueue directly. These are honest dead-code findings: the shipped module is Watchdog plus Packet, nothing more.

files.label: Criticals.java (module)
files.explanation: All behavior sits in the onMotion listener switched on the ModeSetting. Watchdog queues two C04 lifts on every grounded tick; Packet gates three sub-pixel lifts on target presence, onGround and hurtResistantTime versus the Delay NumberSetting. The commented Dev branch and the unused TimerUtil field are the dead-code findings documented in the sections. The file also shows the send path, mc.thePlayer.sendQueue.addToSendQueue for every live lift, which is what makes the wire signature a strict C03 stream with no silent bypass.

files.label: PacketUtils.java (unused silent-send helper)
files.explanation: PacketUtils wraps sendPacket with a silent flag that skips the event bus, and sendPacketNoEvent is the silent variant the commented-out Dev branch would call for its spectate packet. The live Watchdog and Packet modes never touch this class: they queue lifts through the player's sendQueue so every C04 passes through the normal outbound path where other modules and packet listeners can observe it. Including the file documents the contrast, the dead branch's helper versus the live modes' visible queue, which matters because the countering checks key on the lift stream being event-visible.

countering.label: Critical (fall distance divergence and jump phase)
countering.explanation:
NCP's fight.Critical runs whenever the server sees a crit delivered, and its rule 3 is the direct hit on packet lifts: it compares NCP's own fall-distance accounting, derived from real physics, against the fall distance the client's movement claims, and flags when the divergence exceeds 1e-5 while the move's origin is on ground or the touched-ground workaround applies. The Tenacity lifts claim onGround false from a standing position, so the server-side fall distance is fake by construction and the divergence check fires on the first crit after a lift burst. The jump-phase rule 2 also engages for the 0.06 Watchdog lift: a crit delivered while sfJumpPhase sits in 1..maxJumpPhase with no real jump motion is too early in a jump, and NCP's own comment notes SurvivalFly catches the low-jump shape.

The sub-pixel Packet-mode offsets are the honest gap: NCP's envelope machinery never sees them because they fall under the 0.03 min-move, so the coordinate delta is zero to the checker and only the flag is applied. Those modes are fought by the combat-side checks that read the attack itself rather than the movement, which is why the Arc and Hawk entries below matter for the Packet mode specifically.

countering.label: Criticals (attack while physics says onGround)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's combat.Criticals is the simplest counter and the one that bites every Tenacity mode. On each attack it checks Arc's own physics-derived ground state, computed by its MovingListener from the world, not from the packet flag, and flags a critical while onGround whenever that state is grounded and the vertical speed is below 0.37. The Tenacity lifts never move the player more than 0.06 blocks and the sub-pixel Packet offsets move nothing at all, so Arc's ground state stays onGround through the whole burst and every C02 attack that follows a lift is a critical while onGround.

There is no configuration of the module that satisfies this check: only a real 0.42 jump clears the vertical-speed branch, and the module never produces one. The check is also agnostic to the packet split, because it keys on the attack event and the derived ground truth rather than on the C03 stream, which makes it the strongest single counter in this set.

countering.label: SmallHop (mini-lift hop)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's SmallHop exists specifically to catch the mini-hops used to spoof criticals: its docstring says small jumps can be exploited to bypass speed and criticals checks. It flags when the player was onGround, the vertical delta is between 0 and 0.4, the previous delta was non-positive, and no ladder, vine, slime bounce or adjacent solid explains the rise, then punishes and rubberbands. The Watchdog mode's 0.06 lift is squarely inside the 0-0.4 band, so every grounded lift ticks the check and the punishment lands on the first one.

The Packet mode's offsets are the honest boundary: 0.006253453 and 0.002253453 sit inside the band and still flag, while 0.001253453 approaches the 0.001 ground tolerance that the check applies to its onGroundReally test. The sub-0.001 family of criticals offsets is the known pass surface here, which is exactly why the module's smallest lifts are the ones most likely to survive Hawk.

countering.label: NoFall (faked ground claims)
countering.explanation:
Grim's groundspoof.NoFall validates the onGround flag against collision: on a PLAYER_FLYING or ROTATION packet claiming onGround true without a position change, it expands the feet box by the movement threshold, and with no vertical collision it flags, sets back ten blocks and rewrites the claim to false. That is the mirror of what Tenacity does: the module claims onGround false while standing, so the flag-only sub-pixel lifts produce a stream of false ground claims that Grim's post-prediction ground check sees as a player who never lands.

The honest reading is that NoFall's true-claim direction is aimed at the Sigma-style Minis family that spoofs onGround true to avoid fall damage, while Tenacity's false-claim direction surfaces in Grim's prediction pipeline as a consistency problem rather than this specific check. The lift pattern is still visible to the prediction engine through the flag stream, and the position-bearing 0.06 Watchdog lift is subject to the full movement prediction on the next position update.
